Does a database connection still reach its server?

Source: R/util_connection_alive.R
csdb_connection_is_alive.Rd

Returns FALSE when a catalog request on connection shows that the connection lost its server. Use it before cleanup SQL on a connection that MAY have lost its server.

Usage

csdb_connection_is_alive(connection)

Arguments

connection

A DBI connection, or NULL.

Value

TRUE or FALSE. FALSE for NULL, for a closed connection, and when the catalog request gives a condition that shows a lost connection.

Details

DBI::dbIsValid() cannot answer this question. It reports TRUE on an odbc connection whose server ended the session. On such a connection, the first statement gives an R error. The second statement crashes R with a segfault in odbc 1.7.0 with psqlODBC 13.02, and tryCatch() cannot catch a segfault.

The function asks the server whether the table csdb_connection_probe exists. odbc sends that request as an ODBC catalog call, not as a statement. On a lost connection it gives an R error, also after a failed statement. This was measured on 2026-10-22 against PostgreSQL 16.15.

Only a condition whose message shows a lost connection gives FALSE. Any other error or warning of the request gives TRUE, so a live connection still gets its cleanup SQL. See csdb_connection_lost_pattern in the source for the messages.

PostgreSQL releases the advisory locks, the role and the temporary tables of a session when the session ends. Cleanup SQL for them then has nothing to do.

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
csdb_connection_is_alive(con)
#> [1] TRUE
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
csdb_connection_is_alive(con)
#> [1] FALSE
